what_it_does: Running a large language model locally on a smartphone is appealing for privacy and offline use, but the models are far too large to fit in the phone's limited fast memory (RAM). One solution is to store the model on the phone's flash storage (the same kind used for photos and apps) and load only the parts that are active for a given input — a technique that relies on the fact that in many models, only a fraction of the neurons (individual processing units) actually 'fire' for any given input, a property called sparsity. The problem is that flash storage handles long sequential reads efficiently but is very slow when asked to jump around to many scattered locations — and the neurons that happen to be active for a given input are scattered all over the storage in the order they were saved during training. Neuralink solves this by rearranging the neurons on flash before deployment: it profiles which neurons tend to activate together and stores them physically next to each other, turning what would be thousands of scattered random reads into a small number of sequential reads. At runtime, tailored caching logic exploits this new layout to minimize the number of storage accesses needed during inference.
